newsitem.title: USA: Dynamics files suit against WHX.
newsitem.headline: Dynamics files suit against WHX.

text.p: Dynamics Corp of America said it filed a lawsuit accusing WHX Corp of violations of federal securities laws' antifraud provisions in connection with WHX's $45-a-share unsolicited bid.

In its complaint filed in a federal district court in Connecticut, Dynamics also alleged the existence of an "undisclosed group" related to WHX whose holdings of Dynamics' shares, when added to those targeted by the tender offer, would trigger Dynamics' antitakeover rights plan.
Earlier today, Dynamics, a diversified electronic components manufacturer, said its board had formally rejected as "inadequate" WHX's sweetened $45 a share bid.
WHX, the holding company for Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel Corp, originally bid $40 a share, which Dynamics' directors had preliminarily termed "totally inadequate."

WHX later raised the bid, in which it is seeking to buy up to 649,000 shares, which, if added to its current 2.9 percent stake, would give it ownership of 19.9 percent of Dynamics' common stock. It had pledged to buy the remaining shares of Dynamics at the same price.

Dynamics' rights plan constitutes its "poison pill" or antitakeover defenses measure. The plan would be triggered if a group acquired 20 percent or more of Dynamics' outstanding stock. The plan is intended to make it prohibitive for an unwanted bidder to carry out a takeover.

Dynamics said in the lawsuit that its charter requires approval by holders of 80 percent of its outstanding stock, not two-thirds as stated in the WHX tender offer. Changes in Dynamics' bylaws must also be approved by holders of 89 percent of its stock, not 50 percent as stated in the tender offer, it said.

Dynamics said its complaint seeks an order directing WHX to correct its disclosures and an order stopping the bidder from taking any further steps in connection with the offer and WHX's related proxy solicitation, pending compliance with federal securities laws.
